name: e2e
description: Next generation e2e testing framework for web and mobile apps.
one_liner: A tool that lets you describe app tests in plain English, and an AI agent clicks through your website or app to check that things work, instead of a human tester or a programmer writing brittle test scripts.
buyer: A QA lead or founding engineer at a 10-50 person SaaS startup who can't afford a dedicated QA team but needs confidence before every release.
business_use_cases: A startup wires it into CI so every pull request gets agent-driven checkout and signup flow tests before merging.
A QA contractor uses it to write and maintain test suites for multiple client apps without learning each app's internals deeply.
An agency offering 'release confidence as a service' runs it nightly against client staging sites and emails a pass/fail report.

money_ideas.idea: Offer a managed CI testing service: the client describes their critical flows in English, you set up and maintain the e2e suite for a monthly fee.
Sell integration/setup as a one-time service for teams migrating off Selenium or Cypress.

steal_this: This weekend, build a 'test-as-a-service' landing page offering to set up 5 critical-flow agent tests for a startup's app for a flat fee, using this tool under the hood.
